source.title: When Data Falls Short: Grokking Below the Critical Threshold
source.authors: Vaibhav Singh; Eugene Belilovsky; Rahaf Aljundi

record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization in algorithmic tasks and challenges the proposed necessity of weight decay or decreasing weight norms, including reports of grokking below the stated data threshold with distillation.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own outcomes on modular addition and subtraction, grokking, and weight norms. Results cited from other papers are not recorded. Several plots are described in the text without numerical values, so those rows record only the stated qualitative results.
record.test_reason: The study trains one-layer Transformers from scratch on modular addition and subtraction across data fractions and optimizers, giving its own results on grokking and a critical data size (V1, V5). It also argues, using KD runs where norms rise without weight decay, that low-norm bias is not necessary (V5). Most other results concern its KD method rather than grokking arising on its own.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that KD also mitigates catastrophic forgetting in continual pretraining. Add that the authors attribute weight decay's role mainly to mitigating floating-point errors, citing prior work rather than testing it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses one-layer Transformers on modular addition and subtraction with StableMax and KD across differing moduli; it is not a reproduction of the original training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: KD versus no KD; training-data fraction; Adam versus AdamW/weight decay; joint versus continual training.

fits_no_version.finding: Distilling from a model grokked on another modulus accelerates generalization, and enables it below the critical data fraction. This holds for single students and for a larger model trained jointly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Knowledge distillation from a grokked teacher removes or shortens the grokking delay and lowers the critical data size.

fits_no_version.finding: A grokked model further trained on a new modulus generalizes quickly. Without KD it forgets the old task, while KD preserves it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokked models transfer rapidly to related modular tasks without a renewed grokking delay.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: Continual and Compatible Foundation Model Updates (CCFM)
record.problems: Most outcome values are described qualitatively from figures rather than stated numerically. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The study does not report training accuracy alongside test accuracy or systematically quantify how delay changes with data fraction.

untested.parts: Train-accuracy saturation versus test-accuracy timing, and a quantified growth of the delay as the data fraction shrinks.
All of it: no circuit or progress-measure analysis.
All of it: only modular arithmetic, no sweep of initialization scale.
StableMax is used throughout and never compared with softmax. Floating-point and optimizer artifacts are not tested.

missing.what: Scratch-training curves at several data fractions, which could show how the delay changes with data size
Joint cross-entropy training of fM fails whenever p2 is below the critical size
L2 weight-norm trajectory under AdamW, for comparison with Adam

record.verdict_notes: StableMax is used throughout, which may itself remove the weight-decay dependence that softmax collapse creates. The authors do not separate this effect. The threshold is stated inconsistently: 25% or below 'no grokking' in the setup, 'below 30%' for Figure 3, and KD 'grokking' at 25%. No seeds or uncertainty are reported, and results are qualitative descriptions of figures. r7 and r15 are duplicates.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report training-accuracy saturation alongside test accuracy, nor a systematic comparison of optimization delay as training-set size shrinks.
No circuit-formation or memorizing-component measurements, or continuous progress measures, are reported.
The experiments use modular arithmetic; no non-algorithmic datasets or initialization-scale/lazy-to-rich sweep is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
The study does not measure circuit efficiency or test ungrokking; it tests weight decay, weight-norm trends, and generalization below the stated data threshold.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
StableMax is used, but the study does not compare it with softmax or test whether numerical or optimizer artifacts explain the delay.
